title: "Fonts for Presentations: Size, Pairing and Readability" (blog explainer)

brief.story: A clear explainer of the post.

slides.title: Fonts for Presentations: Size, Pairing, Readability
slides.notes: When fonts are right, nobody notices them. When they're wrong, people squint, lose the thread or stop reading. Here's how to choose fonts that stay readable.

slides.title: Pick fonts that survive tough screens
slides.notes: Projectors wash out contrast, laptops shrink everything and video adds compression. Choose fonts with open letter shapes, a generous x-height and solid strokes that hold up in all three.

slides.title: Use reliable fonts and pair them carefully
slides.notes: You don't need a special font, just one that renders the same everywhere. Use one family in two weights, or pair a serif headline with a plain sans-serif body.

slides.title: Set body text at 24pt or larger
slides.notes: If text won't fit at twenty-four point, the slide has too much on it. Cut words, split the slide, or move the detail into your speaker notes.

slides.title: Before and after: make the headline count
bullets: After: "Q2 sales grew in every region except the west"
Six bullets moved to speaker notes
slides.notes: A decorative headline and seven tiny centred bullets became a bold forty-point headline that makes a point, one clearly labelled chart and one left-aligned line.

slides.title: Clear fonts make clearer slide videos
bullets: Check at a small window size
slides.notes: On Pro, a.i. directs your deck, redesigning every slide as an animated scene timed to your narration, but clear type still matters. Try Basic first at powerpoint2vid.com.
